newsitem.title: RUSSIA: St Petersburg summer fuel exports seen at 4.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: St Petersburg summer fuel exports seen at 4.5 mln.

text.p: Russian fuel oil exports through the northern port of St Petersburg are likely to range between 4.25 and 4.50 million tonnes during the 1997 summer shipping season, a Western trader based at the port said on Wednesday.
The volumes, destined for the northwest European market, are likely to be well up on last year's levels, although comparative figures were not immediately available.

"I would calculate that fuel oil exports from St Petersburg will be around 4.5 million tonnes this summer," the trader said, adding that he thought the total would be at the upper end of a range indicated by analysis of deliveries destined for the port.
The total included fuel oil through the port of St Petersburg and through the St Petersburg Oil Terminal, which gets its fuel oil and diesel directly from the neighbouring Kirishi oil refinery.
Fuel oil exports through the Oil Terminal alone this summer are pegged at just over one million tonnes, against year-ago expectations of summer deliveries of 600,000 tonnes.
He said the summer season lasted from May to November. This would give a total average monthly export volume from St Petersburg of between around 600,000 and 650,000 tonnes.

Traders said that 1996 summer fuel oil exports from Russia's northern ports were below both 1995 and expected 1997 volumes because of low water levels in mid-Russia, which prevented barges from being fully loaded.
"This season's expectations are that there will be enough under-water clearance," the St Petersburg-based trader said.
Another factor behind the expected rise in fuel oil exports was an increase in output at the Norsi oil refinery in Nizhni Novgorod, another dealer said.
"This year the refinery should be back to normal operations." he said.
Norsi is a major fuel oil producer, but according to industry estimates output of the product last year fell to around six million tonnes, down 27 percent from 1995 levels.

In addition to St Petersburg, Russian fuel oil is exported through the northern ports of Arkhangelsk and Kandalaksha, which are forecast to export 700,000 and 200,000 tonnes of fuel oil respectively this summer.
"I am looking at exports for around 5.5 million tonnes of Russian fuel oil through Russia's northern ports this season," the St Petersburg trader said.
Early expectations were that there would be roughly an even split between exports of M-40 and M-100 grades.

Fuel oil barges had already started to arrive in St Petersburg, where they are being transferred into storage tankers and loaded on to export vessels, usually carrying between 25,000 and 35,000 tonnes, the trader said.
